The starter is a small mixed community — yeast and lactic acid
bacteria in one jar — and it runs on a schedule. Feed once a day at
room temperature; twice a day if the kitchen is warm.

What you are stabilising is the ratio between the yeasts (which make
gas, the rise) and the bacteria (which make acid, the flavour). Too
little food and the yeast outruns the bacteria; too much and the acid
wins and the loaf goes flat with a sharp tang.

Cold storage slows everything down, and the starter resets after two
or three feeds at temperature. The bubbles are the report: a healthy
starter doubles in six hours.
